chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

We command our young boys to fast when they are seven years old, to the extent they can endure fasting for the day, whether it is until midday or more or less. When thirst and hunger overcome them, they break their fast, until they become accustomed to fasting and are able to endure it. So command your young boys, when they are nine years old, to fast to the extent they can endure, and when thirst overcomes them, they break their fast.

key_terms.بَنِي سَبْعِ سِنِينَ: seven years old (age of accountability start)

ai.seo_question: At what age should children start fasting and how is it gradually introduced according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the pedagogical principle of *tadarruj* (gradualism) in Shia fiqh, distinguishing between the recommended practice of fasting for training (*ta'lim*) at ages seven and nine, and the actual obligation (*wujub*) which typically begins at puberty. It highlights the juristic consensus that children are not yet bound by the full legal penalties of fasting but are trained to endure it progressively, breaking only when physical hardship (*ghalabah*) becomes excessive.
